input.rationale: Section 13.5 correctly vests Developments (including interface coding created solely by Corio) in us and has Commerce One assign any residual claim, and Section 2.8 leaves the vendor's pre-existing Software with the vendor, which is acceptable. However, the "unless" carve-out flips ownership of our own work product to Commerce One merely because it supports that work product on an ongoing basis, with no licence back to us. That is an assignment of Customer IP to the Vendor and fails both the preferred and fallback positions (walk-away territory). The redline deletes the carve-out; a support-purpose licence to Commerce One is offered as a fallback. Separately noted but not flagged: the deferral in Section 13.6/13.5 of ownership of enhancements to the Software itself to future negotiation, and the absence of a general Customer Data ownership statement, which is of limited relevance in this hosting-licence structure.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the carve-out that transfers ownership of Corio-created Developments to Commerce One whenever Commerce One supports them on an ongoing basis, since our playbook does not permit our own work product or IP to vest in the vendor (and there is no licence back to us here). If Commerce One needs rights to maintain those Developments, we can instead grant it a non-exclusive licence to use them solely for support purposes.
proposal.summary: Remove vendor ownership carve-out over Corio-created Developments in Section 13.5.
